title: Malted Milk Chocolate Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Malted milk powder cooked into the custard, milk chocolate melted in and chopped malted milk balls folded through; less sugar.
summary: A take on our classic custard with malted milk powder cooked into the base, milk chocolate melted in and chopped malted milk balls folded through. Creamy, nostalgic and less sweet than you might expect.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
chocolate-coated malted milk balls, roughly chopped and frozen

steps.title: Mix the base
steps.text: In the saucepan, whisk the malted milk powder, sugar and yolks into a thick paste, then gradually whisk in the cream and milk until smooth. Starting with a paste stops the powder forming lumps.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Stir over low heat for 8-10 min until it coats the spatula and reads 77-80 °C. The malt powder can catch, so scrape the base constantly.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: Put the milk chocolate in the heatproof bowl, sieve the hot custard over it, wait 1 min, then stir until smooth. Add the vanilla and salt.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Cool over the iced water and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Churn until thick and add the frozen malted milk balls in the last minute so they stay crunchy.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Pack into the container and freeze for at least 3 h.

tips: Freeze the chopped malted milk balls first, or they soften in the ice cream.
Use plain malted milk powder rather than a chocolate drink mix, which changes the sweetness.
A common mistake is cooking over medium heat to save time; malt scorches easily, so keep it low.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks; the malt balls slowly soften after the first week.
